name: Markwayne Mullin
role: US Senator from Oklahoma (2023–2026), US Representative (2013–2023), US Secretary of Homeland Security (from March 2026)
summary: Republican politician and Trump ally whose record is conservative on taxes, spending, regulation, guns, abortion, same-sex marriage and immigration. He voted to object to the 2020 election results in Arizona and Pennsylvania, backs tariffs and fossil fuel expansion, and has criticised but also worked with union leaders. He is a Cherokee citizen with a mixed record on tribal sovereignty.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Called for ACA repeal and supported market-based health insurance; no statement on universal coverage itself.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Opposed the proposed rise of the federal minimum wage to $10.10.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Opposed federal stimulus spending and stated that excessive government regulation harms job growth.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Stated he opposes increasing tax rates and that "we are taxed enough"; backed the 2017 corporate rate cut.

unions-good.rationale: Criticised unions as putting leaders ahead of workers and backs right-to-work, but later described a friendly working relationship with Teamsters leader Sean O'Brien; mixed record.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Stated that excessive regulations such as EPA rules harm job growth; opposed EPA and OSHA regulations.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Opposed rescheduling marijuana (2023); rated D by NORML.

limit-guns.rationale: Said the Second Amendment leaves "no wiggle room", supports assault rifle ownership; voted against universal background check bills.

empower-police-military.rationale: Voted for higher military spending and said the military should be allowed to use every tool available.

decide-locally.rationale: Backed states leasing federal-land energy rights, state marriage definitions over federal ones, and local control of education.

traditional-family.rationale: Described traditional marriage as a sacred institution.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Stated in 2012 that he opposes same-sex marriage; voted against the Respect for Marriage Act in 2022.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as pro-life; cosponsored the Life at Conception Act; said in a 2022 debate he supports a federal abortion ban without exceptions.

more-religion-public.rationale: In 2024 said he wants the Bible taught to children by believing teachers; limited evidence on public life generally.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Supports completing the border wall, rejects amnesty and criticised catch-and-release; earlier cosponsored raising visa caps (mixed).

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sponsored a measure opposing the UN Arms Trade Treaty, opposed US troops under UN control and criticised the UN in 2025.

free-trade.rationale: Backs tariffs and calls them balancing trade; also supported the USMCA; mixed.

open-borders.rationale: Supports completing the border wall and criticised Biden border policies.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Opposed EPA climate regulations and EV promotion and praised West Virginia v. EPA.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He voted for S.870, whose stated purposes include advancing nuclear energy, and championed funding for a prototype microreactor.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Supports eliminating the inheritance tax and called the death tax a pernicious double tax.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Defended Trump tariffs: countries "got rich over the backs of the workers here in America".

political-violence-never.rationale: He disavows political violence but defends aspects of earlier fighting remarks during the same exchange; the evidence is mixed.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Cherokee citizen who in 2020 joined tribal leaders in a statement on McGirt, but later urged tribes to negotiate with Oklahoma and backed limits on one tribe's sovereignty; mixed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Recorded as saying vouchers break the link between low income and low-quality schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Opposed federal stimulus spending and the $1.9 trillion relief bill; urged balancing the budget.

force-without-un.rationale: Praised the 2025 US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites; no stated view on UN authorisation.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Voted in 2013 to maintain work requirements for welfare recipients and supports workfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: He calls for partnership among business owners, workers and the administration, and for cooperation with organized labor in rebuilding domestic production.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Urged Biden to raise oil and gas production, backed Keystone XL and offshore drilling.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

separated-powers.rationale: He recognises Congress’s lawmaking role but later declines unconditional compliance with judicial orders, calling courts politicised.

death-penalty.rationale: Supports the death penalty, including for killing police officers.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Supported Burwell v. Hobby Lobby and a religious exemption from the ACA individual mandate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Supports personal retirement accounts for Social Security.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Voted in 2014 to aid the Syrian opposition with training and equipment.

non-intervention.rationale: He endorses the strikes on Iran’s nuclear program rather than an absolute prohibition on intervention in another state.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Opposed 2016 guidance on transgender students and restrooms; cosponsored a bill barring transgender women from women's sports.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: His active work securing military installations and new weapons funding supports retaining and strengthening the armed forces.

term-limits.rationale: Recorded as backing a constitutional amendment for congressional term limits.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He defends an officer’s lethal response to a vehicle he describes as a lethal weapon.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: His column argues that law must recognise biological differences between men and women rather than replace them with chosen gender status.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He defends the U.S. attack on Iranian nuclear facilities as accomplishing a necessary preventive mission.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: His defence of lawful private gun ownership and legislation protecting it directly oppose reserving arms to the army and police.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Supports a constitutional balanced budget amendment.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Objected to Biden's student loan forgiveness plan in 2022.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Stated Oklahoma is a strong right-to-work state; recorded as backing right-to-work laws.

voter-id.rationale: He supports requiring voters to prove U.S. citizenship and identifies the SAVE America Act as constitutional.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He argues that Medicaid should concentrate on vulnerable and needy recipients rather than broadly cover able-bodied adults.

notes:
Voted Yea on objections to Arizona and Pennsylvania electors (Jan 2021) and said in 2022 it was absurd that Biden won the most votes; no matching statement exists in the list. Voted for 2022 and 2024 Ukraine aid and worked to pass the 2024 package, but no statement matches. Positions on abortion and same-sex marriage are partly from 2012 statements, confirmed by later votes. Tribal sovereignty evidence is mixed. The mullin.senate.gov site returned HTTP 403 and congress.gov was not used. Most evidence comes from secondary aggregators and Wikipedia.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 14 answers taken from it, 17 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass. Earlier audit consulted only for notes and source leads. Congressional votes are medium confidence; administrative promises are distinguished from implementation. Narrow positions on undocumented immigration do not establish a preference to reduce immigration overall. January 2021 electoral objections do not by themselves settle every statement about democracy. No attempt was made to reach the salience threshold. Final review left universal healthcare, low-paid-worker tax credits and general minority territorial autonomy null because the retrieved evidence concerned narrower proposals. All 490 statement texts, including the ten priority statements, were reviewed against the source set. Technology searches located military R&D and AI security issues, but no clear position on transferring government decisions to algorithms, enhancement, encryption or technological acceleration. Culture searches located personal faith and Cherokee identity, but these alone do not answer the cultural and theological propositions. Priority statements all remain null. Copy validation uses the unchanged validator in a VM with only personPath redirected to this scratchpad; no production audit was replaced.
